_comment: Single source of truth for install.sh / install.bat. Edit versions here only.
commonNotes: whisperx pinned to 3.4.2 — 3.5+ requires torch 2.7.1+, which would silently upgrade the pinned torch above and pull in torchcodec.
pyannote-audio pinned to 3.4.0 — 4.0+ requires torch 2.8+ / torchcodec, same trap, pulled in transitively by whisperx's unbounded requirement.

speechbrain pinned to 1.0.3 — 1.1.0 adds a lazy-import k2 integration that crashes under Python 3.12 when k2 is not installed (hasattr no longer swallows ImportError), triggered by pytorch_lightning's inspect.stack() call while loading pyannote's VAD model.

huggingface_hub pinned to 0.36.0 (the last 0.x release) — 1.0.0 (Oct 2025) removed the deprecated `use_auth_token` kwarg entirely in favour of `token`. pyannote-audio 3.4.0 still calls hf_hub_download(..., use_auth_token=...) internally, so an unpinned install fails with `TypeError: hf_hub_download() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_auth_token'` the first time diarization loads its gated model. https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/issues/1094

notes: Pinned to 2.5.1 — 2.6+ requires torchcodec which has no Windows build.
cu124 requires CUDA 12.4+ drivers (Game Ready 550+ / Studio 555+); backward-compatible with newer runtimes (12.6, 12.8).

extra (Windows): nvidia-cudnn-cu12 pinned to the 8.x line — ctranslate2 (whisperx's transcription backend, pinned <4.5.0) needs cuDNN 8's split libraries (cudnn_ops_infer64_8.dll); cuDNN 9 (the unpinned default) removed them. This works on Windows because torch's own cuDNN DLL is delay-loaded — 'import torch' succeeds even without cuDNN 9 present.

linuxExtra / linuxPostInstall (Linux): torch's CUDA extension hard-links libcudnn.so.9 at import time there (no delay-loading), so the Windows-style cuDNN-8 downgrade breaks 'import torch' outright. Fix used on Linux instead: keep the cuDNN 9 that torch already pulls in, and force-upgrade ctranslate2 to 4.5.0 (adds cuDNN 9 support) after whisperx installs its own <4.5.0-pinned version — a combination reported working by whisperX users/maintainers. See https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX/issues/1158 and https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX/issues/954.
Same 2.5.1 pin as CUDA — 2.6+ requires torchcodec which has no Windows build.
macOS has no CUDA hardware, so it always installs this set, but from the default PyPI index (no --index-url) since download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu does not publish macOS wheels.

onnx._comment: Used only by scripts/export_onnx_models.{bat,sh} — an optional, separate step run after install.{bat,sh}, not part of the base install. Exports Whisper to ONNX for RB.VideoTranslator.WhisperOnnx (native C#, see that project's .csproj) instead of being locked to CTranslate2's CUDA-or-CPU-only backend. Diarization (pyannote/speechbrain) is NOT converted — it still runs on whisperx/torch regardless of this flag. Nothing Python-side runs inference against the exported model anymore, so unlike before this section has no runtime execution-provider package to install — see 'dotnet.notes' below for how the C# side handles GPU/NPU/CPU provider selection instead.
notes: onnxruntime pinned to 1.20.1 for the export step — onnxruntime 1.27.0 (latest as of writing) has a bug in transformers/io_binding_helper.py: TypeHelper.ort_type_to_torch_type() builds its ort-to-torch dtype map unconditionally on every call, including a 'tensor(int4)': torch.int4 entry. torch 2.5.1 (pinned above) has no torch.int4 attribute (that's a newer torch dtype), so merely loading any ORTModel via ORTModelForSpeechSeq2Seq.from_pretrained() raises AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'int4' — regardless of whether int4 tensors are ever used. 1.20.1 predates this and works cleanly.

Export MUST run with plain 'onnxruntime' installed, not 'onnxruntime-directml' — optimum's fix_dynamic_axes step (run right after export) gates on is_onnxruntime_available(), which checks importlib.metadata for a package literally named 'onnxruntime'. onnxruntime-directml is a separate PyPI distribution that happens to provide the same importable 'onnxruntime' module, but doesn't satisfy that metadata check, so export fails with a misleading 'pip install onnx onnxruntime' error even though an onnxruntime-compatible package IS installed.
optimum 2.2.0 removed the old 'optimum[exporters]' extra — ONNX export moved to the separate 'optimum-onnx' package (pip install optimum-onnx), not an extras flag.

ORTModelForSpeechSeq2Seq.save_pretrained() only writes the ONNX graphs + config — it does NOT save the tokenizer/feature-extractor. The export script must separately load WhisperProcessor.from_pretrained(whisperModel) and call processor.save_pretrained() into the same output folder, or the exported folder can't be loaded standalone later.

RB.VideoTranslator.WhisperOnnx (mel spectrogram + BPE tokenizer + decode loop) deliberately references only Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime.Managed (types, no bundled native runtime), never plain Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime or a provider-specific package — every onnxruntime NuGet flavor (Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime, .DirectML, Intel.ML.OnnxRuntime.OpenVino, ...) ships its own runtimes/win-x64/native/onnxruntime.dll under the same path, so referencing two of them in one project (or one consumer's transitive closure) makes NuGet silently pick one at asset-resolution time with no build warning — observed picking the CPU-only build over DirectML's, silently disabling GPU acceleration. Each consumer brings exactly one native provider package: RB.VideoTranslator.Core (WhisperOnnxTranscriberService, DirectML GPU→CPU) uses Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime.DirectML; a separate NPU-only executable would need to use Intel.ML.OnnxRuntime.OpenVino instead, never both in the same project.

Confirmed on this dev machine's hardware (Intel AI Boost NPU + NVIDIA/Intel GPUs): DirectML's device_filter/device enumeration never surfaces the NPU at all (it's not a D3D12/WDDM device on this hardware) — only Intel's OpenVINO execution provider (device_type='NPU') can reach it. OpenVINO can't see the NVIDIA GPU either. There is no single provider that covers NPU+all-GPU-vendors the way the old Python onnxruntime-directml path assumed.
